question: Is the intentional 64 KiB and 250 ms limit acceptable for the legacy Urbit cookie-finalization compatibility path after live evidence confirms it against a real ship?
rationale: The patch deliberately trades an existing unbounded compatibility behavior for a finite login window, and repository policy treats fallback and operator-visible behavior changes as compatibility-sensitive even when they fix a real stall.

options.title: Accept the bounded compatibility window
options.body: Merge after redacted current-head live evidence shows normal Urbit cookie acquisition still succeeds while a stalled body returns promptly.

options.title: Adjust the bound with owner evidence
options.body: Choose a different fixed cap or deadline if a supported Urbit deployment demonstrates that the proposed window rejects a valid login flow.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Leave the existing behavior in place if no bounded compatibility window can be supported by real Urbit evidence.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded compatibility window
recommendation.body: Merge after redacted current-head live evidence shows normal Urbit cookie acquisition still succeeds while a stalled body returns promptly.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior work is the clearest available provenance for the Tlon authentication and SSRF boundary affected by this fallback change.
